rule_parts.example: m_state.age_sec >= 1 : buy on a print once the coin is 1 s old.
rule_parts.summary: The print that triggers the buy. Every condition must hold on that print.
rule_parts.title: Buy on

rule_parts.example: m_state.liquidity_sol >= 14 : only when the pool holds 14+ SOL.
rule_parts.summary: Must also hold at that moment. If one fails, the rule keeps watching the coin.
rule_parts.title: Only if

rule_parts.example: m_crowd.unique_ix_templates @working >= 4 : give up on coins with fewer than 4 working templates.
rule_parts.summary: Checked on the print that would buy. If one fails, the rule stops watching this coin.
rule_parts.title: Only if, else give up

rule_parts.example: token + event age_sec >= 1 : decide once, on the first print after 1 s.
rule_parts.summary: token: only the coin's first event print may buy; slot: only the first event print of each slot.
rule_parts.title: One chance

rule_parts.summary: Buy this percent of the pool's SOL instead of the fixed amount, so our own price impact stays the same.
rule_parts.title: Size as % of pool

rule_parts.summary: Named conditions, written once and used by name in any line. A signal holds when any of its groups holds (every condition of that group).
rule_parts.title: Signals

rule_parts.summary: Sell lines checked first, in every stage.
rule_parts.title: Always

rule_parts.example: early (until age 20 s) -> late -> ride (30 s) -> hold.
rule_parts.summary: The steps after the buy. The position starts in the first stage; each stage has its own lines and may have a deadline.
rule_parts.title: Stages

rule_parts.summary: Lines checked on every print and every 200 ms tick while in this stage, top to bottom; the first that holds acts.
rule_parts.title: While in this stage

rule_parts.example: ends at age 20 s, then late.
rule_parts.summary: When the stage ends: at a coin age, after time held, or after time in this stage. At the deadline the 'at end' lines run once, then the rule moves to 'then' (default: the next stage).
rule_parts.title: Deadline

rule_parts.summary: Lines checked once, when the deadline is reached. A checkpoint.
rule_parts.title: At the deadline

rule_parts.summary: If every condition holds: sell (all, or a percent of the first buy's bag) and/or move to another stage.
rule_parts.title: Line

rule_parts.summary: Shortcut for an always line: sell when m_position.pnl_pct reaches this.
rule_parts.title: Take profit %

rule_parts.summary: Shortcut for an always line, checked before everything: sell when m_position.pnl_pct falls to minus this.
rule_parts.title: Stop loss %

rule_parts.example: cooldown 30 s, at most 3 buys per coin.
rule_parts.summary: After a normal sell, wait this long and watch the coin again, up to a number of buys per coin.
rule_parts.title: Buy again

rule_parts.summary: Do not buy while another rule holds this coin. With two exclusive rules, the higher priority wins.
rule_parts.title: Exclusive

builtin.name: bundled
builtin.summary: Wallets whose first buy landed in a slot where 3+ wallets first bought with one ix shape.

tags.example: volume = program 9ddjzq or a 3-print cluster or the creator, sticky. Then m_flow.buy_sol @!volume = what outsiders bought.

fields.example: "program": ["Axiom Trade"] : every Axiom trade, whatever its instruction list.
fields.summary: The transaction's main program (its first instruction past compute budget, system, token, ATA and memo) is one of these. Catches every build a tool ships.
fields.title: Program

fields.summary: The transaction's exact ordered instruction list is one of these, optionally pinned to its fee preset (CU limit, CU price, tip).
fields.title: Exact ix shape

fields.summary: The transaction's coarse template (program|CU|ATA|N|S|F) is one of these. The only matcher, with program, the slot and wave families can read.
fields.title: Ix template

fields.summary: The instruction list contains one of these markers (a mechanism or a retail router).
fields.title: Contains marker

fields.example: ["Axiom Trade", "Photon"] : every trade that did not come through those routers.
fields.summary: The instruction list contains NONE of these markers: everything except them.
fields.title: Lacks marker

fields.summary: The wallet the venue credited is one of these addresses.
fields.title: Wallet

fields.example: true : the dev's own buys and sells.
fields.summary: The trader is the coin's creator.
fields.title: Creator

fields.example: {"min_prints": 3, "sol_tol_pct": 10} : the 3rd of three matching 0.5 SOL buys in one slot.
fields.summary: The trade is the Nth or later print in one slot with the same ix shape, side and fees, its SOL within P % of the first. Checked last.
fields.title: Same-slot cluster

fields.example: "sell" : a dump list judges sells only.
fields.summary: Only buys, or only sells, can carry the tag. Absent = both.
fields.title: Side

fields.example: true : a wallet caught in a volume cluster stays volume for its later trades.
fields.summary: A wallet that carried the tag once carries it for the rest of the coin.
fields.title: Sticky

fields.example: true : @!volume then means outside buyers only.
fields.summary: A wallet that buys in the creation slot and matches nothing counts on NEITHER side for the rest of the coin: it is the dev's birth bundle or a sniper, not the audience.
fields.title: Ignore creation-slot buyers

tags.summary: A tag is a named trade list. It splits every coin's trades in two: @name = the trades that carry it, @!name = the rest.
